panels.title: Registered frames

targets.expr: count(shareframe_frame_active{serial_number=~"$frame"})

panels.description: Frames in the database, whether or not they have ever reported.

panels.title: Frames reporting

targets.expr: count(count by (serial_number) (count_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} [$__range])))

panels.description: Distinct frames that sent a telemetry heartbeat in the range.

panels.title: Silent frames

targets.expr: count((time() - shareframe_frame_last_seen_timestamp_seconds{serial_number=~"$frame"}) > 900) or vector(0)

panels.description: Registered frames whose Frame.last_seen is older than 15 minutes. The heartbeat interval is 5 minutes. Counts against the database roster, so it no longer depends on what happens to be in the log range.

panels.title: Never seen

targets.expr: (count(shareframe_frame_active{serial_number=~"$frame"}) - count(shareframe_frame_last_seen_timestamp_seconds{serial_number=~"$frame"})) or vector(0)

panels.description: Registered frames with no Frame.last_seen at all - they have never checked in.

panels.title: Unhealthy

targets.expr: (count(last_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} | regexp `log - b'(?P<payload>\{.*\})'$` | line_format `{{.payload}}` | json | label_format healthy=`{{ if eq .health_state "ok" }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}` | unwrap healthy [$__range]) by (serial_number)) - sum(last_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} | regexp `log - b'(?P<payload>\{.*\})'$` | line_format `{{.payload}}` | json | label_format healthy=`{{ if eq .health_state "ok" }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}` | unwrap healthy [$__range]) by (serial_number))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Frames whose most recent heartbeat reported health_state other than ok. health_state is not stored in the database, so this only covers frames that reported inside the range.

panels.title: Service down

targets.expr: sum(last_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} | regexp `log - b'(?P<payload>\{.*\})'$` | line_format `{{.payload}}` | json | label_format service_down=`{{ if or (eq .dashboard_running "false") (eq .display_running "false") (eq .update_running "false") (eq .websocket_running "false") }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}` | unwrap service_down [$__range]) by (serial_number)) or vector(0)

panels.description: Frames whose last heartbeat reported dashboard, display, update or websocket not running.

panels.title: Reboots in range

targets.expr: sum(max_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} | regexp `log - b'(?P<payload>\{.*\})'$` | line_format `{{.payload}}` | json | unwrap boot_count [$__range]) by (serial_number) - min_over_time({job="backend", serial_number=~".+", serial_number=~"$frame", fw_version=~"$fw"} | regexp `log - b'(?P<payload>\{.*\})'$` | line_format `{{.payload}}` | json | unwrap boot_count [$__range]) by (serial_number))

panels.description: Fleet-wide boot_count increase over the range.

panels.title: Fleet roster
panels.description: Every registered frame, straight from the database. One row per frame by construction: public_serial_number is unique, so nothing here can duplicate or go missing when a frame changes address or firmware. Last seen is the Frame.last_seen column, refreshed by websocket traffic as well as heartbeats, so it can be newer than Last heartbeat below.

panels.description: One row per registered frame, newest values. Identity and Last seen come from the database, so a frame appears even when it reported no telemetry in the range - legacy firmware sends only ip and version, so those rows are identity-only. Grouping is by serial_number alone, and the range queries are collapsed to their newest bucket, so a frame cannot occupy more than one row. Last seen tracks websocket traffic too, so it can be newer than Last heartbeat.

panels.title: Websocket connections

targets.expr: sum (count_over_time({job="backend", logger="websockets.frames"} |= "New connection accepted" [$__interval]))

panels.description: Fleet-wide. These lines identify frames by database id, not serial, so the frame filter does not apply to them.

targets.expr: sum by (close_code) (count_over_time({job="backend", logger="websockets.frames"} |= "Connection disconnected" | regexp `with code (?P<close_code>\d+)` [$__interval]))

panels.description: 1000 is a clean close, 1006 an abnormal drop.

panels.title: Stale connections reaped
